blocker.summary: r477 (Piste A of the approved plan) tested r476's timing hypothesis for the (shader, modification) mismatch blocking real native-probe content and refuted it: re-running the same sealed route at --duration 20 (vs r476's 60) produced the IDENTICAL modification pairing for both targeted vertex shaders (0A6D1DD7767FDF27->0x1, C049A8C9E556F129->0x900000000), despite a two-thirds-shorter capture window. Also established the two other sealed 'longstart' routes (60s pure boot, no input -- a priori ideal for matching the native probe's zero-input state) are unusable with the current dump-shader flag combo: they lack the required campaign-new-game/post-campaign-intro-skip capture markers run_gate.py enforces. Rereading draw_pinned() confirmed the mismatch is structural, not a resolution-logic bug: vertex_high depends only on draw.primitive_type==0x08 (decoded straight from the guest PM4 stream), so this is likely two different UI screens reusing the same vertex shader programs with different primitive types, not a bug in native's own PM4 primitive_type decode -- though that hasn't been directly verified either way. Named for r478: (1) trace draw.primitive_type directly in the native probe (not just derived vertex_high) to determine whether this is a real native PM4-decode bug (fixable without oracle) or a genuinely different game screen (would need a new sealed route -- an oracle budget decision, not to be taken unilaterally given how much has already been spent on this campaign); (2) Piste B (commit the stabilized native backlog, r433-r477) and Piste C (HUD guard-rail) from the approved plan, both independent of this track.
